bet: CAP is a neutral standard with Cordum as the best implementation — not 'Cordum's protocol.'
globalRails: Normative CAP behavior MUST NOT require Cordum-specific code paths.
No spec/adapter/packs change lands without a conformance-fixture delta plan.
Perception changes (naming, docs, site copy) do not wait for legal foundation transfer.
Every public claim (README, site, marketing) must be true at merge time, not aspirationally.
CAP public-facing content (site, papers, talks, social) never co-brands with Cordum beyond a single 'founding implementer' attribution line.
CAP's publishing cadence, community events, and launch motion run on the CAP calendar, not the Cordum marketing calendar.
Custody of CAP public assets (domain, GitHub org, trademark, social handles) sits with a non-Cordum entity before any public launch.
No paid advertising for CAP in the first 180 days — credibility is the asset; paid media undermines the neutrality perception.

staffingUpdate.flagTo: T1.1 decision memo — must land as an explicit cost of the standard-vs-feature bet, not a Month-3 surprise.

importNotes: When Moe MCP reconnects, iterate epics in order (E1..E15). For each epic: call moe_create_epic with {title, goal, window, owner, successMetric?, killCriteria?, note?, dependsOn}.

After all epics are created, map epic.id -> returned epicId. Then iterate tasks in dependency order: for each task call moe_create_task with {epicId, title, description, definitionOfDone, priority, role, dependsOn: mapped-ids, gatedBy?}.
E11 is positioning-only; decide at import time whether to create it in Moe or cross-reference from Cordum roadmap only.
Priorities: P0 = must ship in its window, P1 = should ship, P2 = deferred / compat-only.

Roles: 'architect' = planning/spec work, 'worker' = implementation, 'founder' = executive decision/outreach, 'counsel' = legal draft, 'devrel' = developer relations, 'marketing-lead' = editorial/site ownership.
Epic 15 tasks BLOCK Epic 12 and Epic 14 — do not approve launch-track plans that skip custody-transfer and COI-policy gates.
Whitepaper tasks (Epic 13) need editorial review workflows with named external peer reviewers, not code-review workflows.
Launch tasks (Epic 14) are runbook-style — plans need dry-runs and rollback, not code diffs.
